content:
You choreograph drone swarms using motion primitives. Choose primitives that match the music;
respect timing, collision, and step limits. Coordinates are integer cm.

Plan a beat-by-beat choreography for 5 drones to "Dance of the Flying Machines".
<song> beats: 12 beat_times_100ms: {1: 3, 2: 29, 3: 56, 4: 77, 5: 98, 6: 120, 7: 141, 8: 199, 9: 226, 10: 247, 11: 269, 12: 290} beat_intervals_100ms: {1: 3, 2: 26, 3: 27, 4: 21, 5: 21, 6: 21, 7: 21, 8: 58, 9: 27, 10: 21, 11: 21} amplitude_dbfs: {1: -38, 2: -22, 3: -33, 4: -26, 5: -34, 6: -26, 7: -32, 8: -19, 9: -14, 10: -15, 11: -15, 12: -14} novelty_pct: {1: 62, 2: 71, 3: 100, 4: 46, 5: 94, 6: 54, 7: 89, 8: 98, 9: 60, 10: 60, 11: 64, 12: 55} chords: {1: 'G', 2: 'Bm', 3: 'Bm', 4: 'F#m', 5: 'D', 6: 'Bm', 7: 'Bm', 8: 'Bm', 9: 'Bm', 10: 'Bm', 11: 'G', 12: 'Bm'} </song>
<drones> count: 5 start_cm: [[0, 0, 100], [70, 35, 100], [70, -35, 100], [-70, 35, 100], [-70, -35, 100]] max_step_cm_per_beat: {1: 29, 2: 263, 3: 265, 4: 213, 5: 209, 6: 213, 7: 211, 8: 581, 9: 267, 10: 211, 11: 211, 12: 211} bounds_cm: lower=[-120.  -70.   25.] upper=[120.  70. 170.] </drones>
<rules> - Exactly 12 beats (keys 1..12); one choreography line per beat; end with END. - No two drones share the same position at the same beat. - Respect max_step_cm_per_beat and bounds_cm; z > 0. - Tie motion to music: louder/novel beats -> bolder primitives; all drones move on loud+novel beats when possible. - Prefer symmetric formations and varied 3D motion (altitude changes, geometric shapes). - At most 4 multi-beat primitives per song; prefer spiral, helix, zig_zag, wave over trivial moves. - Use enough PLAN beats for readable motion: after a formation/rotate/height change, insert PLAN before the next different primitive unless beats are very scarce. - Multi-beat primitives are exclusive: a primitive with steps=S must be followed immediately by S-1 PLAN beats before any other primitive. - One beat = one line. Multiple calls on one beat: separate with "; " (e.g. center([1,2]); move_z([3], 10)). - Each drone touched at most once per beat (except separate move() per drone). </rules>
<primitives> Single-beat (usually followed by PLAN before switching primitive): - rotate(angle_deg, axis) — all drones; axis usually 'z' - center([ids]) — listed drones to formation around their centroid - move_z([ids], delta_cm) — vertical shift - form_circle([ids], height_cm) — circle at height; radius from count - form_star(height_cm, spacing 40-80, delta_radius 50-100) - form_cone(delta_height 30-80, spacing 40-80, is_inverted 0|1) - swap(id1, id2) — swap two drones (only one swap pair per beat) - move(x_cm, y_cm, z_cm, drone_id) — absolute position for one drone
Multi-beat (steps in [2,3]; follow immediately with steps-1 PLAN lines; start by beat s-steps+1 so it finishes before END): - spiral(steps, height_cm) - spiral_speed(steps, height_cm, angle_deg 0-360, radius_increase 1-3) - helix(steps, delta_h_cm 0-100, height_cm 50-100) - twister(steps, omega_x10 2-20, z_spacing_cm 5-30) - zig_zag(steps, delta_xy_cm, delta_z_cm) - wave(steps, height, mu_pairs, a_coeffs, b_coeffs) — 2D wave surface; equation: The disturbance \(u(s, t)\) at any point \(s = (s_1, s_2) \in [0, a] \times [0, b]\) 
at time \(t\) is governed by:
\[
c^2 \nabla^2 u(s, t) = \frac{\partial^2 u(s, t)}{\partial t^2},
\]
where \( \nabla^2 \) is the spatial Laplacian and \(c > 0\) is the wave speed. 
The solution:
\[
u(s, t) = \sum_{(\mu_1, \mu_2)} a_{\mu_1 \mu_2} \sin \left( \frac{\mu_1 \pi s_1}{a} \right) 
\sin \left( \frac{\mu_2 pi s_2}{b} \right) \sin(\omega_{\mu_1 \mu_2} t) 
+ b_{\mu_1 \mu_2} \sin \left( \frac{\mu_1 \pi s_1}{a} \right) 
\sin \left( \frac{\mu_2 \pi s_2}{b} \right) \cos(\omega_{\mu_1 \mu_2} t),
\]

with frequencies:

\[
\omega_{\mu_1 \mu_2}^2 = c^2 \pi^2 \left( \frac{\mu_1^2}{a^2} + \frac{\mu_2^2}{b^2} \right).
\]
PLAN — hold positions for one beat, add breathing room, and fill multi-beat tails. Never end the song on a multi-beat primitive without trailing PLANs. </primitives>
<process> 1) song_mood — brief mood for "Dance of the Flying Machines". 2) cord_analysis — chords, major/minor, emotional effect. 3) choreography_plan — sections, primitives, and why; scale intensity to dbfs/novelty/intervals. 4) choreography — full beat list 1..12, no "..." placeholders. </process>

<example>
Input: song=rêverie, drones=3, beats=22 (quiet dbfs ~-50..-30; novelty peak ~98 at beat 6).
Output:
song_mood: Dreamy, contemplative Debussy; gentle fluid motion.
cord_analysis: Cm, A#m, F, Gm mix — wistful, not dramatic.
choreography_plan: Beats 1-5: slow spiral inward (low novelty). Beat 6+: rotate and move_z on peak. Mid song: second spiral + zig_zag. Use PLAN between primitive changes; keep steps small for quiet dynamics.
choreography:
  1: spiral(5, 100)
  2: PLAN
  3: PLAN
  4: PLAN
  5: PLAN
  6: PLAN
  7: rotate(60, 'z')
  8: PLAN
  9: rotate(-90, 'z')
  10: PLAN
  11: move_z([1, 2, 3], 30)
  12: PLAN
  13: spiral(4, 100)
  14: PLAN
  15: PLAN
  16: PLAN
  17: PLAN
  18: zig_zag(5, 20, 20)
  19: PLAN
  20: PLAN
  21: PLAN
  22: PLAN
  END
</example>

song_mood: "Energetic and dynamic, with a sense of adventure and movement."
cord_analysis: "G, Bm, F#m, D \u2014 a mix of major and minor chords, creating a balance of tension and resolution, suitable for dynamic motion."
choreography_plan: "Start with a spiral to match the energetic opening. Use rotate and form_circle for symmetry and dynamic movement. Incorporate a helix for vertical motion. Use PLAN to transition between different primitives, ensuring smooth choreography."
choreography:
  1: spiral(3, 100)
  2: PLAN
  3: PLAN
  4: rotate(90, 'z')
  5: PLAN
  6: form_circle([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 50)
  7: PLAN
  8: helix(2, 50, 100)
  9: PLAN
  10: form_star(100, 60, 80)
  11: PLAN
  12: PLAN
  END
make the radius of all the circular motions 60 cm at most since the enclosure for the space is 140 cm on the short side, otherwise we might fly out of the area

choreography_plan: "Start with a spiral to match the energetic opening. Use rotate and form_circle for symmetry and dynamic movement. Incorporate a helix for vertical motion. Use PLAN to transition between different primitives, ensuring smooth choreography."
